verdict.rationale: Instinct is itself an autonomous personal assistant you text or call, and it acts on your behalf: booking rides, handymen and medical appointments, making purchases, and following up on dropped threads (instinct-docs-1, -3, -4, -9, -10). Multiple hands-on testers confirm they handed it real work — travel booking, restaurant reservations, phone calls placed from an iMessage request, email follow-ups, ordering pizza, and proactive appointment booking (instinct-comm-1, -2, -9, -11, -17). The main caveat is execution reliability, which affects trust but not whether delegation works: it sent an email without checking first, made unwanted or wrong bookings that cost fees, was slower than a rival, and got bot-blocked on some sites (instinct-comm-6, -13, -18, -19). Missing for 10: consistent, reliable execution of delegated actions (it acted without confirmation and booked wrongly) and fewer bot-blocking and speed problems.
